result: Full test of 5.7.10 on portable VS Code 1.144.0 (the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). Two findings: (1) liveServer.settings.host does not touch the listening socket - Helper.generateParams hardcodes host '0.0.0.0' and Config.getHost is used only for the browser URL - so with host 127.0.0.1 the server still listens on 0.0.0.0:5501 (netstat, extension-host pid) and is reachable from the LAN; already open upstream as #3091 (created 2025-03-02, no comments), so not filed; (2) the cors description promises Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * but the live-server middleware is cors({origin:true, credentials:true}): no ACAO without an Origin, and Origin: http://example.com is echoed with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true - filed https://github.com/ritwickdey/vscode-live-server/issues/3334. Correct as documented: static serving with text/html, text/css and image/svg+xml types plus charset; 404 body Cannot GET <path>; the reload script is injected into HTML (case-insensitive extension) and into SVG (live-server's own injectCandidates include </svg>), never into CSS or plain text; directory index (index.html) and serve-index listing otherwise (ws_client3.js listed); URL-encoded space, non-ASCII café, query string, HEAD (CL set, no body), Range bytes=0-9 -> 206 with Content-Range, If-None-Match -> 304; ../../../ gets 403 and root=/ls_probe/sub confines serving (outside path 404); mount [['/mnt','ls_probe/css']] serves the css at /mnt/style.css; file 'spa.html' is a 404-only fallback mounted after the static handler (missing path -> 200 spa content, real css still served); headers object adds X-Probe and Cache-Control verbatim; ignoreFiles ['**/*.css'] suppresses the css change while the html change still reloads; fullReload true turns a css change into a full 'reload' instead of 'refreshcss'; live reload verified with a websocket client (connected, reload on html, refreshcss on css, full reload on css with fullReload); port fallback works but takes about 6 s and bumps by +1 (9560 taken -> setting 9561, 445 -> 446), not the "random port" the 5.6.0 changelog promises; goOffline really closes the socket (ECONNREFUSED 1.5 s later); a stop followed by a start needs about 1.2 s (StopServer has an internal 1000 ms wait) or the start is lost. Then measured: https with a self-signed certificate made for localhost and 127.0.0.1 (openssl, PEM certificate plus PKCS#8 key) -> https 200 text/html serving the file's content, while the same path over plain http failed to connect, so the https block really changes the listener; AdvanceCustomBrowserCmdLine was pointed at a recorder .cmd that appends its arguments to a file, so the browser launch is observable WITHOUT opening a browser - it captured https://127.0.0.1:5503/ls2/site/index.html for the https run and https://10.0.0.56:5503/ls2/site/index.html once useLocalIp was true, and that LAN address served 200 as well; CustomBrowser splits its value on ':' (appModel.js), so a Windows path cannot be used there and the recorder has to go through AdvanceCustomBrowserCmdLine; changeWorkspace is real and drivable - in a two-folder .code-workspace the goOnline/changeWorkspace flow opens a folder quick pick, selecting the second item and accepting served work2 (/only2.html 200, /only1.html 404), accepting the first item and going online again switched the root back to work (/only1.html 200, /only2.html 404), and an unanswered pick leaves the server down with a TypeError logged from workspaceResolver.js (workspaceFolders.find(...).uri). Boundary, with evidence rather than a skip: ChromeDebuggingAttachment only appends --new-window --no-default-browser-check --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=<extension dir> when the browser name is chrome or blisk, so those flags exist only in a launched Chrome's command line; Chrome is installed on this machine, so running it would open a real browser window and a debug port, which the audit's no-side-effects rule excludes - the branch is cited in appModel.js instead.

prettier.disableLanguages is declared but never read, so it has no effect: https://github.com/prettier/prettier-vscode/issues/4015. Format Selection formats the whole file when the selection starts at offset 0 (rangeStart 0 is falsy in 'rangeEnd && rangeStart'): commented with the cause on the open issue https://github.com/prettier/prettier-vscode/issues/3567

Full test of 0.12.2 on portable VS Code 1.144.0 (the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). Five defects, all cause-read: (1) $fileNameWithoutExt returns the FULL ABSOLUTE PATH for a file with no extension (getCodeFileWithoutDirAndExt's regex /.*[\/\\](.*(?=\..*))/ needs a dot; verified live: probe_noext -> c:\Users\donal\tools\vscode_portable\work\cr_probe\probe_noext, documented value is the base name); (2) $workspaceRoot resolves to the code file's directory instead of the workspace folder on the first run after activation when code-runner.cwd is set (initialize() returns at the cwd check before _workspaceFolder is computed, and getWorkspaceRoot falls back to codeFileDir; verified after a reload: c:\...\cr_probe\ while the folder is c:\...\work, and it silently becomes the right value after any earlier run without cwd); (3) $dir is quoted WITH its trailing backslash ("...\cr_probe\"), so on Windows every argument after it merges into one token - receipt argv showed `D:c:\...\cr_probe" DT:... F:... N:... NE:... DL:c:` as a single argument (quoted backslash before the closing quote escapes it in CommandLineToArgvW); any native executor using `$dir <something>` is affected; (4) a selection run with runInTerminal true leaves tempCodeRunnerFile.js in the source folder (fs.unlinkSync lives only in the output-channel close handler; 126-byte file left behind after the run); (5) code-runner.stop does nothing in terminal mode (_isRunning is set only in executeCommandInOutputChannel, so stopRunning() no-ops; the heartbeat file kept growing 25 -> 33 lines after the stop). Correct as documented: default run of the active file (node, cwd = workspace root without fileDirectoryAsCwd, [Running] command / [Done] code and seconds in the Code output channel), cwd rules 1-3 (code-runner.cwd, fileDirectoryAsCwd, workspace root), executorMapByGlob (overrides the language map, exact basename and *.js), defaultLanguage fallback for a language with no executor, respectShebang true (#!node) and false (falls through to defaultLanguage), the other placeholders ($fileName, $fullFileName, $dirWithoutTrailingSlash, $driveLetter, dotted basename a.b.js -> a.b), temporaryFileName + languageIdToFileExtensionMap (probeTmp.probe, deleted after an output-channel run), ignoreSelection (whole file, no temp file), saveFileBeforeRun and saveAllFilesBeforeRun (disk verified), clearPreviousOutput, runInTerminal (terminal named Code, correct cwd, program output in the terminal) and executorMapByFileExtension (consulted only when the language has no executor; fires for plaintext .txt; the shipped default object already maps .vbs -> cscript //Nologo, and a user executorMap object REPLACES the shipped defaults rather than merging). Tail round 2026-11-13 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 (vscode-mcp 0.8.4): Run By Language quick pick verified - it lists the executorMap keys and accepting a language runs it (receipt-proven). showRunCommandInEditorContextMenu, showRunIconInEditorTitleMenu and showStopIconInEditorTitleMenu each verified both ways through the AX tree (editor menu item count 25->24 with the setting off; title buttons 'Run Code (Ctrl+Alt+N)' and 'Stop Code Run (Ctrl+Alt+M)' present only with their setting on, the stop one only while codeRunning). showRunCommandInExplorerContextMenu verified both ways with a real right-click on the explorer row (computer-use-mcp indexed click, mouse_button right): 'Run Code Ctrl+Alt+N' heads the 15-item menu with the setting on, absent from the 14-item menu with it off. preserveFocus verified live in output-channel mode: with true a Return keypress after the run landed in the editor (buffer went dirty, extra line); with false the same keypress went to the Code output channel (its text field turned patchable with the run log) and the buffer was unchanged. Not tested: showExecutionMessage=false (it only gates appendLine into the output channel, which has no read API - L424-449); app insights. Full test of 3.24.1 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 with vscode-mcp 0.8.4 (self_test 12/12 first; the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). 26 commands are registered. Two text-editing commands verified exactly: rainbow-csv.Align on "name,city,age / alice,NY,30 / bob,San Francisco,4" produced "name , city         , age / alice, NY           ,  30 / bob  , San Francisco,   4" - every column padded to its widest cell, text left-aligned and the numeric column right-aligned, with a single space kept after each comma; rainbow-csv.Shrink trimmed the padding from "a  , b  , c / 1  , 2  , 3" to "a,b,c / 1,2,3". rainbow-csv.CSVLint reports NOTHING through VS Code diagnostics for a file whose rows have 3, 2 and 4 fields - not a defect: the extension keeps its lint results in an internal map and shows them on a status-bar button, and extension.js contains no createDiagnosticCollection at all, so the lint surface is an API gap (status-bar tooltip only). Full test of 0.18.2 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 with vscode-mcp 0.8.4 (self_test 12/12 first; the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). Applying .editorconfig works exactly: with indent_size = 8 a new line indents to 8 spaces (editor default is 4), and root = true is honoured - a child .editorconfig carrying only indent_style and root = true left indent at the editor default 4, while removing that root line let the parent's [*.js] indent_size = 2 apply (2 spaces). On-save properties work on the DISK bytes: with end_of_line = crlf, trim_trailing_whitespace = true and insert_final_newline = true, saving a dirty file trimmed the trailing spaces from every line and rewrote it with 0D 0A endings (hex dump) and a single final newline. Gotcha worth knowing: save_file on a clean document writes nothing, so those properties appear not to work until the document is dirty. EditorConfig.generate was tested both ways - with editorconfig.generateAuto at its default true it wrote a settings-derived file into the folder passed as the command argument (indent_style space, indent_size 4, end_of_line crlf, charset utf-8, trim false, final newline false, CRLF separators), and with generateAuto false it wrote the shipped out/DefaultTemplate.editorconfig byte-identically (673 characters). ONE DEFECT FILED: https://github.com/editorconfig/editorconfig-vscode/issues/500 - with files.eol explicitly set ("lf" or "crlf") the generated file is corrupt, every line joined by the literal text "lf"/"crlf" instead of a newline and the end_of_line line missing, because eolKey holds the setting name rather than an EOL string and both eolMap[eolKey] and settingsLines.join(eolKey) consume it; verified for both "lf" and "crlf", and the auto path (files.eol unset) is correct. Tail cleared 2026-11-13 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 (reinstalled 0.18.2, indent measured by the spaces a `tab` command inserts on a fresh line): section globs beyond [*]/[*.js] all apply - [*.{foo,bar}] brace expansion -> indent_size 3 on .foo and .bar but not .baz, [Makefile] exact-name -> 5, [deep/**] -> 6; roots nested more than two deep work - root = true in a/b/.editorconfig (depth 3) blocked a/.editorconfig's indent_size = 8 so a/b/c/nested.txt fell back to the editor default 4 while a/x.txt got 8; charset conversion works on real files - charset = utf-8-bom wrote EF BB BF before the content on save, charset = utf-16le decoded the file as UTF-16LE on open (abc -> U+6261) and saved it back as FF FE + UTF-16LE bytes; insert_final_newline = false held - a file saved with no trailing newline stayed without one (control: the = true case added it last round). Spec note: keys before the first [section] header are ignored - a/.editorconfig written without [*] applied nothing until the section was added.

Full test of 3.2.0 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 with vscode-mcp 0.8.4 (self_test 12/12 first; the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). Decoration-only extension, so the API shows none of its work: verified by capturing the editor window (PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT) and counting exact RGB pixels per configured tag background, the bounding box naming the line. Verified as documented: a line comment whose tag is the first non-blank text after the delimiter is decorated (#FF00FF, line 1), the same with spaces before the tag (#00FFFF), a tag that is not the first token is not (#00AAFF = 0), a tag inside a string is not (#00FF00 = 0), a tag following /* on the same line in a block comment is not (#FF0000 = 0), a line inside a plain /* */ block is (#0000FF), a line inside /** */ after the leading * is (#7F00FF), matching is case-insensitive (configured Todo matches // TODO), multilineComments false removes plain block decoration (#0000FF 2127 px -> 0 after the reload the README requires, a CSS block also 0), and highlightPlainText true decorates a tag that is the first non-blank character of a .txt line while a later tag on the next line stays undecorated (bbox confined to line 1). Settings changes took effect only after a window reload, as the README says (pixel counts identical before it). One defect, filed: multilineComments false does NOT stop JSDoc (/** */) decoration in apex/javascript/javascriptreact/typescript/typescriptreact - the JSDoc line kept its #7F00FF background (2162 px) with the setting false, because findsJSDocComments returns highlightMultilineComments || highlightJSDoc and applyLanguage sets highlightJSDoc for those languages, while the README promises multiline comments are presented without decoration - https://github.com/aaron-bond/better-comments/issues/590. No defect beyond the filed one. The four text styles and the two colour forms were then measured separately, each with one colour per tag and a fixture whose four lines carry identical text so captures are comparable. Underline: the tag run gains a horizontal line 100 px long at y=143, the LAST row of that line's band (135-143). Strikethrough: the same 100 px line but at y=156, the middle of its band (154-160) - the same tool, a different row, which is what tells the two apart. Bold: same text and colour, 192 px over 12 rows plain versus 303 px over 39 rows bold, i.e. thicker strokes with no slant. Italic: still 12 rows and 176 px, but the per-row x windows shift (top row starts at 455 and the bottom at 453, where plain sits at 454 for both), a slant without thickening. Theme colour: a tag whose "color" is {"id": "editorError.foreground"} painted exactly the colour forced through workbench.colorCustomizations (#00FF7F), so the id indirection is honoured. rgba background: "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)" over the measured editor background #121314 produced #89090A behind the text (985 px), i.e. a 50 percent composite with 1-LSB rounding, not the transparent fallback. Languages: the same tag decorated in python (63 px, "# ! python comment") and in html (56 px, "<!-- ! html comment -->"), so the language table covers js, css, plaintext, python and html.

Toggle bold/italic/strikethrough/code on a selection inside the markers adds a second layer (*word* + Ctrl+I becomes bold): https://github.com/yzhang-gh/vscode-markdown/issues/1592. Table formatter rewrites tables inside fenced code, indented code, HTML comments and math blocks: https://github.com/yzhang-gh/vscode-markdown/issues/1593

Full test of 0.62.1 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 with vscode-mcp 0.8.4 (self_test 12/12 first; the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). Diagnostics compared by rule code and message on a file built to break several rules: MD041 ("First line in a file should be a top-level heading"), MD022 twice on the same heading line (blanks above and below are separate violations), MD032, MD012 ("Expected: 1; Actual: 2"), MD009 ("Expected: 0 or 2; Actual: 1") and MD047 - and no MD013, which is the documented exception ("all rules are enabled except MD013"); the bundle agrees (its default config is {MD013:false}). Config plumbing works: with .markdownlint.json {"MD041": false, "MD013": {"line_length": 40}} MD041 disappeared and MD013 appeared as "Expected: 40; Actual: 107". markdownlint.fixAll edited the document exactly as the rules promise - blank lines inserted around the heading and before the list, the double blank collapsed, the trailing space removed, a single final newline added - leaving only MD041, which has no fix; re-running left nothing else. The extension also registers as the Markdown formatter: with [markdown].editor.defaultFormatter pinned, editor.action.formatDocument applied the same fixes (MD022, MD009, MD032 -> text "# Title

Text with trailing spaces

- item
") with zero diagnostics afterwards and no Configure Default Formatter dialog. markdownlint.toggleLinting removed all diagnostics and restored them. markdownlint.run "onSave" behaved as documented: an unsaved trailing-space edit produced no diagnostics, saving produced MD009. No defect found. Note for anyone scripting it: markdownlint.fixLine is NOT in the command palette (only fixAll, lintWorkspace and openConfigFile are contributed) - it is the target a quick-fix code action calls with (line, fixInfo), so invoking it without those arguments is a no-op, and invoking it with a malformed fixInfo deletes the line. Tail round 2026-11-13 cleared the remaining items. lintWorkspace runs as a task ("Lint all Markdown files in the workspace", $markdownlint problem matcher): Problems badges appeared workspace-wide including files never opened (bad1.md 4, bad2.md 3, bad3.md 1, cli2/longline.md 1 problems; clean files correctly absent). markdownlint-cli2 config files are honoured per directory: .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc {"config":{"MD013":{"line_length":40}}} produced "Expected: 40; Actual: 65" only under that folder while an identical long line outside it stayed clean; a malformed config logs "Unable to parse JSONC content" to the markdownlint output channel and linting continues. customRules via .markdownlint-cli2.cjs work: a parser:"none" rule flagged its marker at the right line with its detail text; onError takes ONE object argument ({lineNumber, detail, ...}) - positional args throw "Value of 'lineNumber' passed to onError is incorrect" - and rule modules are cached, so editing a rule file needs a window reload before it takes effect. Code-action quick fixes through the UI verified: editor.action.codeAction on an MD032 line opened the Action Widget listing "Fix this violation of MD032/blanks-around-lists", "Fix all violations of MD032 in the document", "Fix all supported markdownlint violations in the document" and config/help entries; acceptSelectedCodeAction applied the selected fix. markdownlint.fixAll is per-document ("Fix all supported violations in the document"), not workspace-wide: it fixed MD022/MD009/MD047 on one file and MD012 on another while unfixable MD041, MD033, MD013 and the custom ZZPROBE diagnostic all survived untouched.

Full test of 1.30.0 on portable VS Code 1.146.0 with vscode-mcp 0.9.1 (workspace trust disabled; the 2026-10-28 row was a smoke test). All ten commands exercised live through the generated command tools against fixture repo work/gg_probe (master+feature, 3 commits): git-graph.view opened/reused the webview view and registered the repo (log shows Started watching repo); git-graph.fetch ran git fetch --all then a full re-read (log); git-graph.openFile with a correctly encoded git-graph://file.txt?<base64 {filePath,commit,repo,exists}> URI opened work/gg_probe/a.txt in the editor; git-graph.version showed its dialog (Copy/Cancel, dismissed via dismiss_dialog); git-graph.clearAvatarCache, resumeWorkspaceCodeReview, endAllWorkspaceCodeReviews and endSpecificWorkspaceCodeReview all returned cleanly; git-graph.removeGitRepository stopped the repo watch (log) and git-graph.view with {rootUri:{$uri:...}} re-registered it. git-graph.addGitRepository always calls showOpenDialog - args are ignored - so the success path needs a human to pick a folder; the dialog opened and Cancel dismissed it cleanly (verified twice). Two agent-side traps recorded, not extension defects: openFile with a file:// URI or a malformed git-graph URI (query must be base64 JSON produced by encodeDiffDocUri; a bare git-graph:file.txt?query URI parses with an empty query and decodeDiffDocUri throws, leaving run_command pending:true behind an undismissable error toast), and view with a bare string arg throws Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace). No defect found in the extension itself.
